departments.title: AI Strategy
departments.description: Define the organisation's AI ambition, target outcomes, principles, operating model and roadmap, starting from business outcomes rather than products.

skills.name: ai-maturity-assessment
skills.description: Diagnoses an organisation's current AI maturity across strategy, people and adoption, knowledge, governance, platform and delivery capability, and value measurement, using observed evidence rather than self-scored opinion, and maps the result to a CopilotForge archetype. Use when a programme is starting, when leaders disagree about how ready they are, or when a strategy refresh needs an honest baseline.

skills.name: ai-operating-model
skills.description: Designs the target operating model for AI - who decides, who builds, who supports and who owns value - choosing a central, hub-and-spoke or federated shape to suit the edition and archetype, and placing the Centre of Excellence within it. Use when AI work is spreading without clear ownership, when leaders ask how AI should be organised, or before a CoE is chartered.

skills.name: ai-roadmap
skills.description: Builds a prioritised, sequenced AI roadmap across the Adopt AI, Build with AI and Scale AI journeys and the lifecycle stages, showing dependencies, capacity, foundations and review points against the agreed outcomes. Use when leaders need a plan for the next twelve to twenty-four months, when initiatives compete for the same people, or when an existing roadmap has drifted from its outcomes.
skills.platforms: copilot-chat, m365-copilot, m365-agents, copilot-cowork, copilot-code, copilot-studio, ai-foundry, power-platform

skills.name: strategic-outcomes
skills.description: Turns an AI ambition into three to five measurable business outcomes, a short set of AI principles and an explicit statement of where AI will not be used, with clear expectations of the executive sponsor. Use when leaders say they want an AI strategy, when a programme has activity but no agreed outcomes, or when a sponsor needs to explain why the organisation is investing in AI.

departments.title: Opportunity Management
departments.description: Create a disciplined path from business problem to prioritised and governed initiative, including the decision about whether AI is the right answer at all.

skills.name: ai-suitability
skills.description: Decides whether a framed business problem should be solved with AI at all, and if so which pattern fits - Copilot Chat, a Cowork task, an agent, Copilot Code, a Foundry solution or plain automation - with the reasoning recorded. Use when an idea arrives at intake, when a team has already picked a tool, or when a sponsor asks why AI is preferable to process change or training.
skills.platforms: copilot-chat, m365-copilot, m365-agents, copilot-cowork, copilot-code, copilot-studio, ai-foundry, power-platform

skills.name: opportunity-prioritisation
skills.description: Scores and balances a backlog of framed AI opportunities on value, feasibility, risk, readiness of knowledge and ownership, and strategic fit, and shapes a portfolio of quick wins and strategic bets. Admits nothing without an owner, problem, outcome, risk tier and suitability decision. Use when ideas outnumber capacity, when a steering group must choose what goes next, or when the backlog has lost its link to outcomes.

skills.name: problem-framing
skills.description: Turns a raw idea or tool request into a framed business problem with a named business owner, affected roles, current cost, expected outcome and baseline, and politely sends solution-first requests back to the problem. Use when an idea arrives at intake, when someone asks for an agent or Copilot feature before saying what is wrong, or when a pilot cannot say what it was meant to improve.

skills.name: risk-classification
skills.description: Assigns a progressive risk tier from 0 to 4 to an AI opportunity or solution by rating impact, reach, data sensitivity and autonomy, then derives the minimum governance posture and the reviewer gates it must pass, and re-classifies when scope changes. Use when an idea has a chosen pattern, when a solution is about to be shared more widely, or when someone asks which reviews a build needs.
skills.platforms: copilot-chat, m365-copilot, m365-agents, copilot-cowork, copilot-code, copilot-studio, ai-foundry, power-platform

skills.name: scale-or-stop
skills.description: Makes the evidence-based decision after a pilot or first release to scale, iterate, pivot or stop, judged against the value hypothesis, adoption, quality and cost, and treats a well-evidenced stop as a success. Use when a pilot reaches its review date, when a sponsor wants to roll a solution out wider, or when a live initiative has been running for months without anyone deciding its future.
skills.platforms: m365-copilot, m365-agents, copilot-cowork, copilot-code, copilot-studio, ai-foundry, power-platform

departments.title: Value Realisation
departments.description: Define baselines, measures and ownership so adoption and deployed solutions create demonstrable value.

departments.title: Programme Management
departments.description: Mobilise and govern a coherent adoption, delivery or transformation programme.

departments.title: Copilot Adoption
departments.description: Design and run organisation-wide or business-unit Microsoft AI adoption programmes, from readiness and scenarios through launch, reinforcement and measurement.

skills.name: adoption-measurement
skills.description: Defines how Copilot adoption is measured across usage, capability, behaviour change and business outcomes, with baselines set before launch, team or role-level reporting above a minimum group size, and feedback loops that change the programme. Use when setting adoption measures, when a sponsor asks whether Copilot is working, or when someone proposes tracking individual usage.

skills.name: adoption-readiness
skills.description: Assesses whether an organisation or business unit is ready to adopt Microsoft Copilot across sponsorship, licences assigned versus used, IT-led technical enablement, data and permissions hygiene, approved-use guidance, support and communications, and records the gaps to close before launch. Use when licences have been bought or are about to be, before a launch date is fixed, or when early use has stalled.

skills.name: launch-plan
skills.description: Plans a phased Copilot launch with onboarding by persona, executive and manager enablement, reinforcement through office hours and Champions, a support model and a feedback loop that keeps improving the programme. Use when readiness gaps are known and a rollout needs sequencing, when a big-bang launch is being proposed, or when a launch happened but nothing followed it.

skills.name: scenario-discovery
skills.description: Segments the workforce into personas such as desk, hybrid and frontline workers, discovers role-based Copilot scenarios with business owners, prioritises them by value and frequency, and builds a scenario catalogue with prompt patterns that users can verify. Use when planning what people will actually do with Copilot, when usage is generic and shallow, or when a new team or role joins the rollout.

departments.title: Champions
departments.description: Create evidence-led Champion programmes that turn curiosity into capability and capability into contribution, with clear boundaries on what Champions do and do not do.

skills.name: capability-framework
skills.description: Defines the Champion capability levels - verified Chat capability, productivity capability and agent capability - each with observable evidence and an evidence rubric, and offers two routes to each level, structured learning or direct evidence submission. Use when setting what a Champion must be able to do, when Champion status needs to mean something, or when experienced colleagues want to skip training.

skills.name: champion-challenges
skills.description: Designs practical Champion Challenges in which a verified Champion solves a real team problem using safe, approved tools, producing reusable assets such as prompt patterns or guides, and routing any larger opportunity to intake. Use when Champions are ready to apply their capability, when the community needs fresh practical work, or when a challenge idea needs checking for safety and scope.

skills.name: champion-programme-design
skills.description: Designs an evidence-led Copilot Champions programme - purpose, charter, operating boundaries stating what Champions do and do not do, executive sponsorship, a time commitment agreed with managers, and community design. Use when starting a Champion network, when an existing network has become an unpaid help desk, or when Champion status has come to mean attendance rather than capability.

skills.name: evidence-assessment
skills.description: Sets up fair, consistent assessment of Champion evidence against the capability rubric, by trained assessors who assess the evidence rather than the person, give useful feedback, handle resubmissions and appeals, and never rank anyone. Use when Champion submissions start arriving, when assessors disagree, or when someone challenges a decision about their evidence.

skills.name: recognition-and-progression
skills.description: Designs how Champions are recognised and progress - join, verify capabilities, complete a challenge, earn recognition and keep contributing - with renewal so status stays current, a regular programme health check and Champion metrics reported at programme level only. Use when designing Champion recognition, when status has gone stale, or when a sponsor asks whether the Champions programme is healthy.

departments.title: Learning and Skills
departments.description: Create role-based learning, practice, assessment and progression pathways.

departments.title: Change and Communications
departments.description: Build sponsorship, communications, manager engagement, behavioural reinforcement and change readiness.

departments.title: Knowledge Management
departments.description: Make organisational knowledge discoverable, owned, current, classified and suitable for AI grounding.

departments.title: Microsoft 365 Copilot
departments.description: Help organisations introduce Microsoft Copilot as an everyday working capability.

departments.title: Microsoft 365 Agents
departments.description: Turn organisational knowledge and repeatable information needs into appropriately scoped, owned and tested agents with a managed lifecycle.

skills.name: agent-release-readiness
skills.description: Runs the release gate for an agent, confirming owner, support route, sharing scope matched to risk tier, reviewer evidence, communications, monitoring, review date and retirement criteria, and registers the agent in the solution register. Use when an agent has passed testing and someone wants to share it, when its audience is about to widen, or when a live agent has no clear owner.
skills.sources: ms-copilot-studio-zoned-governance, ms-copilot-studio-security-governance, ms-managed-environments, ms-agent-builder, ms-coe-starter-kit, ms-copilot-studio-guidance

skills.name: agent-testing
skills.description: Builds a proportionate test plan and a small evaluation set of real user questions with expected answers, covering groundedness, refusal and out-of-scope behaviour, permission trimming across different users and regression after change, against a threshold the business owner agrees. Use when an agent is ready for testing, before widening its audience, or after its instructions or knowledge change.

skills.name: agent-use-case-design
skills.description: Turns an approved agent opportunity into an agent brief covering audience, purpose, scope and exclusions, instructions approach, knowledge sources, actions, the build-or-reuse decision, owner, support and success measures. Use when an idea has passed suitability as an agent, when a maker wants to start building, or when an existing agent needs its scope rewritten.

skills.name: knowledge-source-readiness
skills.description: Assesses each knowledge source an agent will ground on for owner, currency, accuracy, permissions and oversharing, classification and review cycle, and records a ready, ready-with-conditions or not-ready verdict. Use when an agent brief names its sources, when a maker wants to add a site or library as knowledge, or when an agent starts giving outdated or surprising answers.

departments.title: Copilot Cowork
departments.description: Design safe, effective delegation of complex work with explicit context, checkpoints and review.

departments.title: Copilot Code
departments.description: Translate desired outcomes into governed software prototypes and production-ready engineering work.

departments.title: Copilot Studio
departments.description: Design and deliver low-code and enterprise agents with appropriate actions, data, ALM and lifecycle controls.

departments.title: Microsoft Foundry
departments.description: Engineer specialist and custom AI solutions where configured agents are insufficient.

departments.title: Automation
departments.description: Combine AI with deterministic workflow automation where repeatability and integration matter.

departments.title: AI Engineering
departments.description: Provide pro-code engineering patterns shared across custom AI solutions.

departments.title: AI Architecture
departments.description: Select appropriate patterns and define target architecture across Microsoft 365, Power Platform, Azure and data services.

departments.title: Security and Privacy
departments.description: Reviewer-class department that assesses identity, access, data exposure, connectors, privacy and retention for AI solutions and blocks release while material risks are unresolved.

skills.name: connector-review
skills.description: Reviews the connectors, actions, tools, MCP servers and APIs an agent or automation uses, covering user versus maker authentication, least privilege, data policies, data leaving the tenant and confirmation for write actions, and classifies each finding as blocking or advisory with a fix. Use when an agent gains an action or tool, when a flow uses a new connector, or when a maker shares a connection.
skills.platforms: m365-agents, copilot-studio, power-platform, ai-foundry, entra, azure

skills.name: data-exposure-review
skills.description: Reviews what content an AI solution can reach and reveal - oversharing, permissions, sensitivity labels, the agent's sharing scope, web and public knowledge, and where outputs travel - and classifies each finding as blocking or advisory with a fix. Use when an agent or Copilot rollout reaches its security gate, when a maker adds a large knowledge source, or when sensitive content surfaces in answers.
skills.platforms: m365-copilot, m365-agents, copilot-studio, sharepoint, purview, entra

skills.name: privacy-assessment
skills.description: Assesses personal data in an AI solution for lawful basis, purpose limitation, transparency, data minimisation, retention of prompts, responses and transcripts, DPIA screening under UK GDPR and ICO guidance, and people-related uses, classifying findings as blocking or advisory. Use when an agent or AI solution processes personal data, when transcripts are kept, or when AI outputs inform decisions about people.

departments.title: Responsible AI
departments.description: Reviewer-class department that identifies impact, accountability, human oversight, unacceptable uses and mitigating controls.

departments.title: Data Governance
departments.description: Ensure the data used by AI is appropriately owned, classified, accessible, lawful and of sufficient quality.

departments.title: Evaluation and Quality
departments.description: Reviewer-class department that defines evaluation sets, acceptance criteria, failure analysis and release evidence for probabilistic systems.

departments.title: Platform Governance
departments.description: Govern environments, makers, connectors, agents, deployment, licensing and portfolio visibility.

departments.title: AI Operations
departments.description: Operate deployed agents and AI solutions throughout support, monitoring, review, improvement and retirement.

departments.title: Design Authority
departments.description: Reviewer-class department that challenges inappropriate platform choice, unnecessary AI, fragile architecture and unsupportable designs.

departments.title: AI Centre of Excellence
departments.description: Orchestrate a business-owned AI Centre of Excellence covering charter, operating model, team, governance, opportunity flow, knowledge, cadence, RACI and value measurement.

skills.name: coe-cadence
skills.description: Sets the meeting cadence and terms of reference for an AI CoE - steering, portfolio and design review, community and value review - with agendas, inputs, outputs and a decision log, sized to the edition. Use when a new CoE needs its forums set up, when meetings have become status updates that decide nothing, or when decisions are being taken in corridors and nobody can find them later.

skills.name: coe-charter
skills.description: Drafts the charter for an AI Centre of Excellence - purpose, scope across the six pillars, principles, sponsorship, decision rights and what the CoE is not - or the lighter terms of an AI working group for a small organisation. Use when management asks for an AI CoE, when an existing group has drifted into a reporting forum or request queue, or when a sponsor needs one page to agree before people are appointed.

skills.name: coe-governance-model
skills.description: Writes a proportionate AI governance framework and acceptable-use starter - progressive risk tiers 0 to 4 with minimum controls, a solution register, ownership and lifecycle controls, and reviewer gates - so low-risk experimentation is not blocked. Use when there is no approved AI policy, when departments are building agents with no register or owner, or when governance is so heavy that people work around it.
skills.platforms: copilot-chat, m365-copilot, m365-agents, copilot-cowork, copilot-studio, power-platform, purview, entra
skills.sources: ms-copilot-studio-zoned-governance, ms-copilot-studio-security-governance, ms-managed-environments, ms-coe-starter-kit, ms-copilot-privacy, ms-responsible-ai, nist-ai-rmf, ico-ai-data-protection, iso-iec-42001

skills.name: coe-kpi-framework
skills.description: Builds a KPI framework and scorecard for an AI CoE across adoption, capability, portfolio flow, quality, governance and value, each measure with a baseline, target, source and business owner, reported at team level. Use when a sponsor asks how they will know AI is working, when reporting relies on licence counts or hours saved, or when the steering group needs a scorecard before its first value review.

skills.name: coe-operating-model
skills.description: Designs how an AI Centre of Excellence actually runs - the core team and business roles, a central, hub-and-spoke or federated shape chosen by edition, and the flow from intake through the opportunity lifecycle to the right delivery route, linked to the Champion community. Use when a charter is agreed and the CoE now needs people, routes and a workable flow, or when an existing CoE has become a bottleneck.

skills.name: coe-raci
skills.description: Builds a role-based RACI for AI work across the opportunity lifecycle, governance decisions, knowledge ownership, release and value, with exactly one Accountable per activity and the business accountable for outcomes. Use when nobody can say who approves an agent, when IT is being held to account for business benefits, or when a new CoE needs clear responsibilities before its first steering meeting.

departments.title: Organisation Tailoring
departments.description: Turn an organisation profile into a recommended edition and maturity archetype, a scaled programme, an ownership map and a transformation pack.

skills.name: ai-profile-intake
skills.description: Creates or validates an organisation profile - size, business units, regulatory context, Microsoft estate, current AI use, knowledge, governance, adoption and delivery capability - by short interview or from a file, capturing only what tailoring needs and marking unknowns. Use when someone asks for help with an AI programme and no profile exists, when a profile file is supplied, or when circumstances have changed since the last pack.

skills.name: edition-and-archetype
skills.description: Applies the CopilotForge tailoring rules to a validated organisation profile to recommend an edition (starter, scale or enterprise), an assurance overlay and a maturity archetype, citing the rule id behind each, reporting emerging signals and explaining the result to the sponsor before any pack is built. Use when a profile is ready, when a sponsor asks why they got a lighter or heavier programme, or when circumstances change.

skills.name: ownership-map
skills.description: Produces a role-based ownership map for an AI programme from declared roles only - the accountable role for each engaged department and each pack artefact, named owners only where the organisation has declared them, and the capability and capacity gaps to close. Use when a transformation pack needs owners, when a sponsor asks who will do this work, or when nobody can say who owns adoption, governance or agents.

skills.name: transformation-pack
skills.description: Orchestrates a tailored AI transformation pack from a confirmed profile - assessment, target operating model, adoption and Champions programmes, CoE, opportunity process, agent delivery, governance, roadmap, ownership map, templates and success measures - at the depth the edition sets, and explains material changes on refresh. Use when an organisation asks for help adopting Copilot, scaling agents or setting up an AI CoE.
skills.lifecycle: Discover, Envision, Mobilise, Enable, Deliver, Assure, Launch, Measure, Scale, Improve
